subsystems.name: Cost Hamiltonian encoding
subsystems.role: Encodes the objective function of the optimisation problem into a quantum operator whose ground state represents the optimal solution.

subsystems.name: Mixer Hamiltonian
subsystems.role: Drives transitions between candidate solutions so the algorithm can explore the search space.

subsystems.name: Parameterised quantum circuit
subsystems.role: Alternating layers of cost and mixer unitaries with adjustable angles that define the QAOA ansatz.

subsystems.name: Classical optimiser
subsystems.role: Tunes the circuit parameters by minimising the measured expectation value of the cost Hamiltonian.

subsystems.name: Measurement and readout
subsystems.role: Extracts bitstring samples to estimate expectation values and candidate solutions.
parts: projective measurements in the computational basis

subsystems.name: Compilation and error mitigation
subsystems.role: Maps the abstract circuit to native hardware gates and reduces the impact of noise.

buildSteps.title: Map problem to cost Hamiltonian
buildSteps.detail: Formulate the combinatorial optimisation problem as a sum of Pauli terms; the ground state of this operator encodes the optimal solution.

buildSteps.title: Choose a mixer Hamiltonian
buildSteps.detail: Select a mixer (typically a transverse field) that allows transitions between feasible states without violating constraints.

buildSteps.title: Construct the QAOA circuit
buildSteps.detail: Build p layers of alternating cost and mixer unitaries, each with its own parameter angles β and γ.

buildSteps.title: Compile for hardware
buildSteps.detail: Transpile the parameterised circuit into the native gate set of the target quantum processor and schedule operations to respect connectivity.

buildSteps.title: Execute and sample
buildSteps.detail: Run the circuit on the quantum processor, measure the output state in the computational basis, and collect many shots.

buildSteps.title: Estimate the cost
buildSteps.detail: Compute the expectation value of the cost Hamiltonian from the measured bitstring frequencies.

buildSteps.title: Optimise parameters
buildSteps.detail: Feed the expectation value to a classical optimiser, which updates the circuit parameters to reduce the cost.

buildSteps.title: Iterate to convergence
buildSteps.detail: Repeat execution and optimisation until the optimiser converges to a set of parameters that minimises the cost.

buildSteps.title: Decode solution
buildSteps.detail: Measure the final circuit and decode the most frequent bitstring into the problem solution.

prerequisites.tech: Gate-based quantum processors with sufficient qubits and coherence
prerequisites.why: Current devices offer tens to hundreds of qubits, but limited coherence and connectivity restrict circuit depth.
Two-qubit gate errors must be low enough for the repeated layers of a QAOA circuit.
Needed to run the variational loop that tunes parameters between quantum executions.
Essential because current hardware is noisy and full fault tolerance is not available.
Map abstract circuits to hardware-native gates and optimise them for the device topology.

pathway.milestone: Small-scale QAOA demonstrations on 10–100 qubits for toy optimisation problems
pathway.unlocks: Proof-of-principle results and algorithm development on real hardware.

pathway.milestone: Improved error mitigation and higher-fidelity gates enable QAOA on problems with hundreds of variables
pathway.unlocks: Potential quantum advantage for niche combinatorial optimisation tasks.

pathway.milestone: Fault-tolerant quantum computers with logical qubits run deeper QAOA circuits
pathway.unlocks: Solving practical combinatorial problems faster than classical methods.

pathway.milestone: Integration of QAOA with classical solvers in logistics, finance and materials
pathway.unlocks: Commercial adoption of hybrid quantum–classical optimisation workflows.
